note: What the creatures do, the routes through this place, and what a Remix may change.

encounters.name: Ossuary guardians and breach crabs

locked: The buried watch-temple holds the ward that reactivates the Ember road.
Core problem: Protective wards misfire and corrupted creatures threaten the settlement.
open: The key to the vestry sea-chest hangs on a wrapped keeper's neck (searched after the fight).
When the fight in the nave starts, the breach crabs (VI-WT-05) join.
The same faint glow as the harbor crabs: a link the party can notice (flavour only).
A Potion of Healing lies in a rotted satchel among the shells (DC 10 Wisdom (Perception)).

languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak
original.does: Wrapped temple keepers woken by the misfiring wards; they stand in the ossuary niches and loose shortbows into the dark nave at anyone the ward has not recognised.
Comes through the east breach from the flooded cistern when fighting starts in the nave, shells glowing faintly at the joints like the harbor's crabs.

difficulty.tuner_recommends: as built (plays as moderate); not applied unless the map says so

terrain.light: Dark (daylight only at the stair landing; the ward-stones give Dim light near the ward door)
terrain.water: the broken cistern and the sea beyond the breach
rewards: creatures with darkvision against a party without it
terrain.gaps: the rubble gap at the stair is 10 ft; the ossuary door 5 ft; the cistern breach 10 ft

may_change: the read-aloud and GM lines about them
must_keep: the dark nave and the ward-stones' unsure light
guardians who stop anyone the ward has not recognised
the key to the sea-chest on a keeper's neck
the measured difficulty (plays as moderate with the breach crabs, or the GM's target)
creatures from the sea through the breach
the corrupted glow that links them to the harbor

filters.movement: walkers in the nave; swimmers through the breach

remix.freshness: a remix for returning players avoids Skeletons and Giant Crabs

not_simulated: Skeleton: shooting with Advantage at unseen targets in the dark is played; their joining only on hearing the fight is the GM's

routes.when: A character who has seen the road-and-hand carving (the gate arch or the ward door) shows it, traced in dust or on a hand, before the skeletons loose.
routes.success: The keepers lower their bows and step back into their niches: the sign was the temple's own greeting. They stay still unless someone touches the wrapped dead.
routes.failure: The sign means nothing to them made that way; they loose as written.
routes.reveals: The keepers understood Common in life: one rasps, without a voice, the shape of the word 'passage'.
routes.canon: The temple counts passages, never reigns (the vestry tally board, VI-WT-03): the same distinction, shown.

routes.when: The party crosses the nave along the west pillars without light.
routes.success: The party reaches the sealed ward door unseen; the skeletons keep watch on the stair.
routes.failure: A boot scrapes the mosaic; arrows come out of the dark.
routes.cost: The sea-chest's key stays on the keeper in the ossuary.
routes.reveals: Close to the door, the ward-stones brighten toward the champion's hand.
routes.canon: The ward door's recognition still happens; nothing locked is skipped.

routes.when: Before the fight in the nave, someone sees the breach and the water moving.
routes.success: Rubble heaped into the breach keeps the crabs in the cistern; they scrape at it and stay there.
routes.failure: The heap slides into the water and the crabs come over it.
routes.cost: The satchel with the Potion of Healing stays beyond the heap.
routes.canon: Shrinks the temple's fight; the ward door and the ward chamber still wait.

routes.when: The fight in the nave is avoided altogether (the skeletons were passed or calmed).
routes.success: Without the noise of a fight the crabs never come up from the cistern.
routes.failure: Someone splashes at the breach; the crabs come.
routes.canon: The crabs answer noise, not the champion: the ward, not the beasts, is the temple's story.
